images.text:
Grant: So how's life been treating you, buddy?
Adam: Alright, I guess. I'm working pretty hard looking for a job.
Grant: Oh, we've all been there. I'm going to an interview next week.
Adam : It's really tough. I've done so many interviews, I could write an instruction manual about how to do them. I will be going to a few more interviews in the next few weeks.
Grant: Problem is, you haven't been successful at getting a job. I'm not sure your manual would be a best-seller.
Adam : Oh, get out of here! I've learned a lot of good tips and tricks for doing interviews. When is yours?

Grant: I have an interview next Wednesday. I could really use some help.
Adam : Well, the first thing you have to do is do research about the company. You'll learn about the structure and purpose of the company. You'll also see how they set themselves apart from others. You'll impress the interviewer if you give some reasons why you want to work there. I'm going to do a lot more research before my next interview.
Grant: That makes sense. In my last interview, they asked me why I wanted to work there instead of somewhere else. I didn't know what to say.
Adam: The next thing is to find out as much as you can about the role. Some recruiters asked me if I thought the job advertisement was misleading. They explained that the person writing the job description was often not the person you work for. It's possible you will be doing something quite different in the role.

Grant: That's interesting.
Adam: Thirdly, it sounds a bit cliché, but you really have to know your strengths and weaknesses. Employers want you to be self-aware. You have to take a long hard look at what you have achieved, the way you have achieved that result, and the skills you developed along the way. This helps you understand what you're good at. It gives you confidence.
Grant: Sold! I'll be the first person to buy a copy of your manual. When I finish reading it, I will have learned everything I need to know about doing interviews!

The Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tenses

You use the Future Continuous tense to talk about something happening at a particular time in the future.
You use the Future Perfect tense to talk about something that will be complete by a certain time in the future.
Look at the chart for information about the Future Continuous and Future Perfect tenses:
When I finish reading the manual, I will have learned everything I need to know about doing interviews!
Hopefully, by tomorrow I will have decided what to wear for the first day on the job.
At the end of the week the committee will have delivered their report.
I will be going to a few more interviews in the next few weeks.
Next week, my boss will be meeting with me every afternoon.
The CEO will be chairing the shareholder's meeting tomorrow.

The Future with Will, Going to and the Present Continuous Tenses

When you want to talk about the future, but you need to be specific about the circumstances around the event, you can choose from these structures: will + verb, be going to + verb and the Present Continuous tense (subject + v-ing).
Take a look at the chart for an outline of when to use these different tenses and an example of each:
You'll learn about the structure and purpose of the company.
You'll also see how they set themselves apart from others.
You'll impress the interviewer if you give some reasons why you want to work there.
I'm going to do a lot more research before my next interview.
It's possible you will be doing something quite different in the role.
I'm going to an interview next week.
